task.description: Implement the fix design at src/design/fix-ISS-0106.md (validated PASS in Step 2b) for ISS-0106 / GitHub #364. Restructure build.zig test-integration step dependency graph: introduce a barrier Step that aggregates all non-ISS-503 test-integration binaries, remove run_iss503_integration_tests.step as a direct sibling of test_integration_step (currently line ~1258), give run_iss503_integration_tests.step a dependOn edge on the new barrier, then re-attach run_iss503_integration_tests.step to test_integration_step so the umbrella step still surfaces its pass/fail. Also add a short doc comment (documentation only, no behavioral change) near the top of tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig explaining that build.zig now serializes this binary out of the concurrent group, cross-referencing ISS-0106/#364. Do NOT touch test_integration_iss503_step (the already-isolated zig build test-integration-iss503 narrow step) or the concurrency of the other ~19+ binaries relative to each other. Do NOT add retry/sleep/lock-timeout workarounds. Do NOT add advisory-lock hardening (explicitly deferred per the design).
acceptance_criteria: zig build test exits 0 (unit tests unaffected)
The new barrier Step correctly gates run_iss503_integration_tests.step behind all other test-integration sibling Run steps
zig build test-integration-iss503 still works standalone (unaffected)
zig build test-integration runs to completion; ISS-503 binary observably starts only after the rest of the group finishes (verify via timestamps/log ordering in a real run)

TC-DB-01-01 and TC-DB-01-02 in db_integration_test.zig pass under a full concurrent zig build test-integration run (the original acceptance bar from #357), with no new deadlock (40P01) errors involving test_iss503_rls_removal.zig in the log

result.summary: Implemented the ISS-0106 design exactly as specified. build.zig: removed the direct test_integration_step -> run_iss503_integration_tests.step sibling edge; added a new barrier Step (test_integration_others_step, exposed as internal step 'test-integration-others-internal') that aggregates every other test-integration binary's Run step (the ~19+ edges previously on test_integration_step, including the two later-appended exp103/iss0072 edges); the umbrella now depends on a dedicated second Run artifact (run_iss503_integration_tests_after_others, built from the same iss503_integration_tests Compile step) which depends on the barrier, so ISS-503 only starts after every other sibling has finished. During implementation, discovered and fixed a coupling defect in my own first draft: putting the barrier dependency directly on the SHARED run_iss503_integration_tests.step would have made the pre-existing narrow 'zig build test-integration-iss503' step transitively pull in all ~19 other binaries too (violating the design's explicit non-goal of leaving that step unaffected) -- verified via a standalone run before the fix (test-integration-others-internal wrongly appeared in its tree) and after the fix (it no longer does, and 'zig build test-integration-iss503' completes in isolation with exit 0). Added the required doc comment to tests/integration/test_iss503_rls_removal.zig cross-referencing ISS-0106/#364 and naming the barrier step, documentation-only as specified. VERIFIED: zig build exits 0 (multiple times, including after the coupling fix). zig build test exits 0 (all unit tests pass) once a correct BPM_TEST_DB_URL port (5434, per .env; an unrelated squatting container from a different project occupies port 5433) was used -- this env misconfiguration was pre-existing and unrelated to this fix. zig build test-integration-iss503 verified standalone twice: confirmed isolated from the barrier (no test-integration-others-internal in its step tree) and exits 0 (TC-ISS503-01's deliberate pre-flight-guard-trigger test and the other 3 ISS-503 tests all pass). Full zig build test-integration was run 3 times end-to-end against a freshly-migrated, empty-row test database with no concurrent external DB access during each run (runs 3, 4, 5, after diagnosing and working around two unrelated pre-existing environment issues: a stale/wrong BPM_TEST_DB_URL port in the shell, and a latent bug in tests/integration/helpers.zig's markPublicGlobalSkipsApplied() that only manifests when public.schema_migrations is completely empty, which trips the out-of-order-migration guard on a truly virgin DB -- worked around by bootstrapping via `zig build migrate` before any test binary touches a fresh DB, matching how the shared dev/CI test DB is normally kept in a pre-migrated state). All 3 clean test-integration runs show: (a) zero occurrences of iss503/ISS503/test_iss503 in the logs, meaning the ISS-503 binary is correctly gated behind the barrier and never starts until the barrier settles -- direct proof the concurrency window this issue targets no longer exists; (b) the test_integration_others_step barrier itself fails on each run due to genuine Postgres deadlocks (40P01) AMONG the ~19+ other binaries themselves (14, 10, and 4 deadlocks respectively across the three runs) -- a pre-existing condition the validated design explicitly scoped out ('the ~19+ other binaries remain fully concurrent with each other... this design narrows the fix to exactly the one binary'); (c) because the barrier's own failure propagates to the umbrella step under Zig's build-step semantics, TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 still fail on all 3 runs, but the failure signature has changed from ISS-503-involved (the original #357 bug) to others-vs-others (a different, newly-isolated pre-existing issue, filed as ISS-0107/#366 per the No-Issue-Left-Local-Only directive). Could NOT achieve a fully green zig build test-integration run because of ISS-0107, which is outside this fix's validated scope and files_to_change. Marking PARTIAL rather than PASS because the literal acceptance criterion 'TC-DB-01-01 and TC-DB-01-02 pass under a full concurrent zig build test-integration run' was not met end-to-end, even though the specific mechanism this issue targets (ISS-503 racing the rest of the group) is proven eliminated by direct log evidence across 3 independent runs.

issues.description: ISS-0107 (GitHub #366) filed: the test_integration_others_step barrier group (~19+ non-ISS-503 test-integration binaries) deadlocks (40P01) among itself under full concurrent zig build test-integration, independent of and unaffected by this fix. This is why TC-DB-01-01/TC-DB-01-02 still fail end-to-end despite ISS-503 being proven no longer a participant in any deadlock. Confirmed pre-existing (build.zig's diff for this fix never touches the ~19+ other binaries' relative concurrency) and out of this fix's validated design scope.

Two unrelated pre-existing environment issues were diagnosed and worked around during validation, not fixed in the codebase (out of this fix's file scope): (1) the shell's BPM_TEST_DB_URL sometimes points at port 5433, which is occupied by an unrelated 'my-fab' project's exited container -- the correct port per .env is 5434, where this repo's own db_test container actually runs; (2) tests/integration/helpers.zig's markPublicGlobalSkipsApplied() pre-seeds 3 GBL migration rows unconditionally before the real migration loop runs, which trips src/db/migrations.zig's out-of-order-migration guard when public.schema_migrations is completely empty (i.e. a truly fresh/virgin test database) -- worked around by always bootstrapping via `zig build migrate` (which does not call markPublicGlobalSkipsApplied) before any test binary touches a fresh DB. Neither of these blocks ISS-0106's own fix or normal CI/dev usage (the shared test DB is never actually empty in that workflow), so neither was fixed here; flagging for awareness in case a future fresh-environment bootstrap (e.g. a new CI runner) hits the same guard trip.
